response.sql: WITH exam_counts AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) as exam_count FROM Examination WHERE ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID), totals AS (SELECT SUM(exam_count) as total_exams, COUNT(*) as num_patients FROM exam_counts) SELECT ec.ID, ec.exam_count, CAST(ec.exam_count AS REAL) / t.total_exams as share, CAST(ec.exam_count AS REAL) / t.total_exams - 1.0 / t.num_patients as margin FROM exam_counts ec, totals t WHERE CAST(ec.exam_count AS REAL) / t.total_exams > 1.0 / t.num_patients ORDER BY margin DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Examination records with NULL ID are excluded, since they cannot be attributed to a patient
Average share is defined as 1/N (where N = number of patients with examinations), representing the proportion each patient would receive under uniform distribution

alternatives.interpretation: If 'above-average share' should mean above the mean examination count per patient (not as a proportion), show top 10 patients by how much their count exceeds that mean
alternatives.sql: WITH exam_counts AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) as exam_count FROM Examination WHERE ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID), stats AS (SELECT SUM(exam_count) as total_exams, COUNT(*) as num_patients, SUM(exam_count) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) as avg_count FROM exam_counts) SELECT ec.ID, ec.exam_count, ec.exam_count * 1.0 / s.total_exams as share, ec.exam_count - s.avg_count as margin FROM exam_counts ec, stats s WHERE ec.exam_count > s.avg_count ORDER BY margin DESC LIMIT 10
